question: What fluid do endocrine glands use to send their hormones directly to target organs?
explanation: Endocrine glands do not have ducts. They release hormones directly into the blood circulation so they can travel throughout the body. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h1)

question: How do hormone signals from the endocrine system generally compare to nerve signals from the nervous system?

options.A: Nervous system actions are permanent whereas hormones are temporary
options.B: Endocrine responses are slower and longer lasting
options.C: Nervous responses rely on circulating chemical messengers
options.D: Endocrine impulses travel exclusively along nerve fibres

explanation: Chemical signals traveling through the blood take longer to start than electrical nerve impulses, but their effects usually last much longer. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h1)

question: Which brain structure is the main connection between the nervous and endocrine systems?
explanation: The hypothalamus picks up nerve signals and turns them into hormone signals by controlling the nearby pituitary gland. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h2)

question: A woman has weak contractions during the third stage of labor. Which hypothalamic hormone helps strengthen these contractions?
explanation: Oxytocin is released from the back part of the pituitary gland and attaches to uterine muscle to help create strong contractions. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h2)

question: Which nutrient from our diet is needed to make thyroid hormones?
explanation: Thyroid hormones need iodine atoms to form, making a diet with enough iodine essential for their production. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the main job of parathyroid hormone in the body?

options.D: To stimulate sodium retention in the kidneys

explanation: Parathyroid hormone responds to low blood calcium by drawing calcium from bones, helping the kidneys keep more of it, and increasing absorption in the gut. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h3)

question: Which hormone tells the kidneys to hold onto sodium and get rid of potassium?
explanation: Aldosterone is made by the outer part of the adrenal glands and helps the kidneys balance fluids and electrolytes. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which of these is NOT something adrenaline normally does during a sudden stress event?
explanation: Adrenaline actually opens up the airways in the lungs to let in more oxygen during stress, rather than tightening them. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h4)

question: Which specific cells in the pancreas make and release insulin?
explanation: Beta cells produce and release insulin when blood sugar levels go up after eating carbohydrates. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h5)

question: A patient feels dizzy and sweats after missing a meal. Which hormone goes to work to raise their blood sugar?
explanation: When blood sugar drops between meals, alpha cells release glucagon to tell the liver to break down stored glycogen and release sugar. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h5)

question: Which hormone found in early urine or blood tests lets us know a woman is pregnant?
explanation: hCG is produced by the early placenta right after implantation, and it is the hormone standard pregnancy tests look for. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main job of progesterone during pregnancy?

options.A: To trigger the immediate onset of active labor contractions
options.B: To stimulate early follicle development in the ovaries
options.C: To maintain the uterine lining and keep the myometrium relaxed
options.D: To promote direct milk ejection from the mammary ducts

explanation: Progesterone keeps the muscles of the uterus calm and relaxed throughout pregnancy to protect the baby from early birth. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h6)

question: How does a negative feedback loop usually work in the endocrine system?

options.A: It prevents target organs from ever responding to circulating signals
options.B: It suppresses further hormone secretion when blood levels become too high
options.C: It destroys circulating hormones directly inside the bloodstream
options.D: It amplifies hormone release continuously until an external event stops it

explanation: Negative feedback slows down or stops hormone production when levels get high, bringing the body back to its normal balance point. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is a classic example of positive feedback in human reproduction?

options.A: Oxytocin release causing contractions that push the baby against the cervix
options.B: Thyroid hormones reducing the production of TSH from the pituitary gland
options.C: Aldosterone stopping sodium excretion when blood pressure drops
options.D: Insulin lowering blood glucose levels after eating a carbohydrate meal

explanation: When the baby presses against the cervix, it triggers more oxytocin release, which causes stronger contractions, pushing the baby harder against the cervix in a building loop. [learn more](BMP121_U4_T2#BMP121_U4_T2_h7)
